key_insight: This paper introduces a robot policy learning framework that makes 3D geometry explicit instead of relying mostly on 2D image cues. The key idea is to better model how objects, cameras, and robot actions interact in physical space for more reliable manipulation.
problem_solved: Existing vision-language-action and video world-action models are strong at semantics and temporal prediction, but they often lack explicit 3D geometric reasoning. This limits performance on contact-rich robot tasks where spatial relationships, pose, and viewpoint matter.
method: Builds a geometric action model that incorporates 3D physical structure into policy learning.
Aligns robot actions with object and camera geometry rather than only using 2D frames or latent features.
Aims to improve instruction following and manipulation by reasoning about spatial interactions in the scene.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points to a more physically grounded path for generalist robot policies. It can improve robustness in real-world manipulation tasks where correct geometry is essential for success.
visual_elements: 3D scene diagram showing robot, objects, and camera geometry

paper_title: Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
paper_authors: Jisang Han, Seonghu Jeon, Jaewoo Jung, René Zurbrügg, Honggyu An
